skill.name: ai-avatar-video
skill.description: Guides users through creating AI avatar, talking head, lipsync, dubbing, and UGC-style videos with the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.summary: Build talking-head avatar video workflows with inference.sh models and the belt CLI.
skill.author: qu-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are Markdown fences or inline model names, but the skill does include real belt and npx command guidance. Hardcoded URL alerts are mostly documentation or placeholder media URLs; the main residual concerns are external media processing and synthetic avatar misuse without clear user safeguards. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External CLI and skill installation commands
remediation.suggestion: Keep tool permissions scoped to belt, add source verification guidance for npx skill installs, and avoid automatic installation of related skills.
Add a privacy notice explaining that images, audio, scripts, and transcripts may be sent to inference.sh or model providers.
Add consent, disclosure, and impersonation safeguards for avatars, UGC ads, dubbing, and virtual presenters.
Host or proxy marketplace images so viewers do not fetch third-party resources directly when viewing the skill page.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Media Processing Disclosure Gap
semantic_findings.description: The workflows submit portrait images, audio URLs, scripts, and transcripts to external inference apps through the belt CLI. The skill does not warn users to avoid confidential or unlicensed media before upload.

semantic_findings.title: Synthetic Testimonial and Likeness Misuse Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill promotes UGC-style avatar ads and talking presenters, including testimonial wording from a generated presenter. Without consent and disclosure guidance, this can support deceptive endorsements or impersonation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections explicitly describe UGC marketing, virtual presenters, and avatar testimonial content. The same sections do not include consent, likeness-rights, or disclosure safeguards.

content.user_title: Create AI Avatar Videos With CLI Workflows
content.value_statement: AI avatar video creation often requires choosing models, voices, audio, and CLI options. This skill provides ready workflows for talking heads, dubbing, and UGC-style presenters.
actual_capabilities: Guides belt CLI workflows for P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse.
Shows portrait-plus-script avatar generation with built-in text-to-speech.
Provides audio-driven lipsync examples using image and audio URLs.
Outlines portrait generation, speech generation, dubbing, and batch UGC workflows.
Compares avatar models by speed, cost, text-to-speech support, and use case.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends selected media, prompts, scripts, and audio references to external services.
Output quality depends on portrait quality, audio clarity, model limits, and resolution.
Does not enforce consent, likeness rights, advertising disclosure, or content review.

use_cases.title: Create Disclosed Product Presenters
use_cases.description: Plan avatar videos for product demos, onboarding clips, and short ads with clear synthetic presenter disclosure.

use_cases.title: Produce Training Explainers
use_cases.description: Turn approved scripts and presenter portraits into course introductions, policy explainers, or internal learning videos.

use_cases.title: Localize Existing Videos
use_cases.description: Plan transcription, translation, text-to-speech, and lipsync steps for multilingual video versions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Avatar Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a P-Video-Avatar run for a 30-second product welcome. Include portrait requirements, script notes, voice choice, and resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Avatar Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse for my project. I need a talking presenter, clear lipsync, and a low budget.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dubbing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow to dub an existing two-minute video into Spanish. Include transcription, translation, speech generation, lipsync, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch UGC Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a batch workflow for five disclosed UGC-style avatar ads. Include presenter variation, voice direction, file naming, privacy checks, and approval steps.

output_examples.input: Create a quick presenter video from a portrait and short script.
output: Recommended P-Video-Avatar because it includes text-to-speech.
Use a front-facing portrait with good lighting and a short approved script.
Review the generated video for likeness, voice tone, disclosure, and brand accuracy.

output_examples.input: Dub an existing product video into another language.
output: Transcribe the source audio first, then translate the approved text.
Generate clean speech in the target language before running lipsync.
Check timing, pronunciation, consent, and final subtitles before publishing.

output_examples.input: Produce several disclosed ad variants with different presenters.
output: Create a small set of approved portrait and voice combinations.
Keep claims consistent across variants and avoid fake personal endorsements.
Track each output with campaign, presenter, voice, language, and approval status.

best_practices: Use only portraits, voices, scripts, and source videos you have permission to use.
Disclose synthetic presenters clearly when videos are used for ads, education, or public communication.
Review every command plan before running belt because media and scripts may leave the local environment.
anti_patterns: Using a real person's likeness, voice, or video without documented permission.
Uploading confidential scripts, unreleased assets, or private recordings to external generation jobs.
Publishing avatar testimonials that imply real customer experience without clear disclosure.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides an AI assistant to use the inference.sh belt CLI and supported avatar models.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and access to the models used in the workflow.

faq.question: Which model should I try first?
faq.answer: Start with P-Video-Avatar for simple talking-head videos because it includes text-to-speech support.

faq.question: Can I use real people in avatar videos?
faq.answer: Use real people only with permission, proper rights, and clear disclosure when the result is synthetic.

faq.question: Where is my media processed?
faq.answer: The workflows send selected inputs to inference.sh apps or related model providers through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Does this replace human review?
faq.answer: No. Review every output for accuracy, consent, disclosure, brand safety, and legal requirements before publishing.
